# The closed subgroup generated by `U(χ)`, `χ` and `U(χ⁻¹)`

Author: Worker 37.

Let `G` be a smooth affine group scheme over a field `k` and
`χ : 𝔾_m ⟶ G` a cocharacter. This module constructs the closed subgroup `H`
of `G` generated by the image of the morphism

```text
U(χ) ×_k 𝔾_m ×_k U(χ⁻¹) ⟶ G,   (a, t, b) ↦ a · χ(t) · b,
```

and proves the three properties used by the infinite-field rational-lifting
argument in `Langlands.GroupScheme.Dynamic.OppositeEnvelopeLifting`:

- `H` contains `U(χ)`, `U(χ⁻¹)` and the image of `χ`;
- `H` is normalized by `P(χ)` on every relative scheme test;
- over an infinite field, the rational points of `H` are Zariski dense.

It also proves a variant of the published product theorem
`Dynamic.normal_subgroup_product_smooth_surjective` whose normality hypothesis
is weakened to exactly what this subgroup satisfies. All declarations are in
the namespace `Langlands.GroupScheme.Dynamic` and work at an arbitrary
universe `u`. No perfectness, characteristic, reductivity or splitness
hypothesis is used anywhere; infinitude of `k` is assumed only for density.

## The product theorem

`normalized_subgroup_product_smooth_surjective` assumes:

- `G` smooth and affine over `k` with connected underlying space;
- `H` and `P` smooth and affine over `k`;
- a closed subgroup `d : H ⟶ G` and a monomorphism `i : P ⟶ G`;
- `hn`: the range of `d` is normalized by the range of `i`, i.e. on every
  relative test `T`, `g x g⁻¹` lies in the range of `d` whenever `g` is in the
  range of `i` and `x` in the range of `d`;
- `hU`: `Dynamic.unipotent (CommGroupScheme.groupHom (Gm.powerHom _ (-1)) ≫ χ)`,
  the subgroup functor `U(χ⁻¹)`, is contained in the range of `d`;
- `hP`: `Dynamic.parabolic χ`, the subgroup functor `P(χ)`, is contained in
  the range of `i`.

It concludes that the multiplication morphism `H ×_k P ⟶ G`,
`(h, p) ↦ d(h) · i(p)`, is smooth and surjective.

The proof is that of the published `normal_subgroup_product_smooth_surjective`,
which instead assumes full normality of the range of `d` and that `d` contains
the image of `χ`. The normalization hypothesis `hn` gives the actual
conjugation action `AutomorphicAction.ofNormalizedConjugation d i hn` of `P` on
`H`. The factor `s : U(χ⁻¹) ⟶ H` is obtained by factoring the chosen affine
representative `Affine.unipotentHom` of `U(χ⁻¹)` through `d`, using `hU`; the
published theorem obtained it from normality by a contraction argument. The
factor `t : P(χ) ⟶ P` comes from `hP`. The published opposite-cell theorem
`oppositeCellStatement` makes `U(χ⁻¹) ×_k P(χ) ⟶ G` an open immersion, and
`AutomorphicAction.smoothSurjective_of_openCell` then shows that the
multiplication from the semidirect product is smooth and surjective. By
`semidirectHomLift_hom` its underlying morphism is the product morphism of the
statement.

## The generating morphism

In the namespace `OppositeEnvelope`, `G.X.left` is assumed affine, so that the
chosen affine representatives of the dynamic subgroups exist.

- `reversed χ` is the cocharacter `t ↦ χ(t⁻¹)`, written as
  `CommGroupScheme.groupHom (Gm.powerHom _ (-1)) ≫ χ`, exactly the form used
  by the opposite-cell statement.
- `source χ` is `U(χ).X ⊗ (𝔾_m.X ⊗ U(χ⁻¹).X)`, using the representatives
  `Affine.unipotentScheme χ` and `Affine.unipotentScheme (reversed χ)`.
- `point χ a t b` is the point `(a, t, b)` of the source and `map χ` is the
  morphism `(a, t, b) ↦ a · χ(t) · b`, where `a` and `b` are mapped to `G` by
  the representing closed immersions `Affine.unipotentHom`.
- `comp_map` and `point_map` compute `map χ` on points, and `basePoint_map`
  says that the base point `basePoint χ = (1, 1, 1)` maps to the identity.

## Smoothness, connectedness and existence

For smooth affine `G`, `unipotentScheme_smooth`, `unipotentScheme_isAffineHom`
and `unipotentScheme_connectedSpace` show that the representative of `U(ψ)` is
smooth, affine and connected for every cocharacter `ψ`, by the published
`dynamicSmooth`, the closed immersion into `G`, and `dynamicConnected`. With
`smoothConnectedAffineGeometry` each of the three factors of the source is
geometrically integral, affine and of finite type, and
`ImageGeneration.finitePowerGood_tensor` gives the same for the source
(`source_good`).

`exists_generatedImage` applies the published
`ImageGeneration.pointedImageGeneration` to `map χ` and the base point. It gives
an actual `D : GeneratedImage (map χ)` with `D.HasSmoothConnectedGeneration`:
`D.group` is smooth, affine and geometrically connected, and some positive
power map `D.powerMap n` from the `n`-fold power of the source is dominant.
Here `GeneratedImage (map χ)` is a closed subgroup representing
`closedImageEnvelope (map χ)`, the intersection, on every relative test, of
the ranges of all closed subgroups of `G` through which `map χ` factors.

## Containment

`comp_map_mem` says that every point `v ≫ map χ` lies in the range of
`D.inclusion`. Evaluating `map χ` at `(a, 1, 1)`, `(1, 1, b)` and `(1, t, 1)`
gives `unipotent_le`, `reversed_unipotent_le` and `range_cocharacter_le`: the
subgroup functors `U(χ)`, `U(χ⁻¹)` and the range of `χ` are contained in the
range of `D.inclusion`.

## Normalization by `P(χ)`

`conj_comp_map_mem` assumes `G.X.hom` separated. For a point `p` of `P(χ)` and a
point `w` of the source over the same test `T`, it shows that
`p · (w ≫ map χ) · p⁻¹` lies in the range of `D.inclusion`. Let `l` be the limit
of `p` (published `limit`). It lies in `Z(χ)` by `limit_mem_centralizer`, and
`u = p · l⁻¹` lies in `U(χ)` by `mul_inv_limit_mem_unipotent`. Writing
`w ≫ map χ = a · χ(τ) · b`, the group identity

```text
p (a χ(τ) b) p⁻¹ = u · (l a l⁻¹) · (l χ(τ) l⁻¹) · (l b l⁻¹) · u⁻¹
```

reduces the claim to its five factors. `u` lies in `U(χ)`. `l a l⁻¹` lies in
`U(χ)` because `P(χ)` normalizes `U(χ)` (`conj_mem_unipotent`). `l` commutes
with `χ(τ)` because `Z(χ)` is the torus centralizer of `χ`
(`torusCentralizer_gm_eq_dynamicCentralizer`), so `l χ(τ) l⁻¹ = χ(τ)`. Finally
`l` lies in `Z(χ⁻¹)` by `centralizer_le_precomp`, hence in `P(χ⁻¹)`, so
`l b l⁻¹` lies in `U(χ⁻¹)`. All five factors lie in the range of `D.inclusion`
by the containment lemmas.

`isNormalizedBy_parabolic` assumes `G.X.hom` affine and concludes that the
range of `D.inclusion` is normalized by `P(χ)` on every relative test,
including nonreduced tests. Let `b` be the conjugation action of the affine
representative `Affine.parabolicHom χ` on `G`. The orbit core of the range of
`D.inclusion` under `b` consists of the points all of whose conjugates, after
every refinement, stay in that range. The published
`AutomorphicAction.orbitCore_range_isClosedRepresentable` represents this
orbit core by a closed subgroup. `conj_comp_map_mem` shows that it contains the
image of `map χ`. By minimality of the closed envelope
(`closedImageEnvelope_le_of_containsImage`) the whole range of `D.inclusion`
lies in the orbit core, which is the asserted normalization. Full normality of
the range in `G` is neither proved nor needed here.

## Density

- `hasDenseRationalPoints_unit`: the terminal object over `k` has dense
  rational points.
- `finitePower_smooth_dense`: if `V` is smooth over `k` with dense rational
  points, then so is every finite power of `V`. The induction uses
  `finitePowerZeroIso` and `finitePowerSuccIso`, `smooth_tensor`, and the
  published `RationalDensity.HasDenseRationalPoints.tensor` with openness of
  the first projection along a smooth factor.
- `source_smooth`: the source is smooth over `k`.
- `source_dense`: over an infinite field the source has dense rational points.
  The representatives of `U(χ)` and `U(χ⁻¹)` are split unipotent
  (`isSplitUnipotent_of_isRepresentedBy_unipotent`), hence have dense rational
  points (`RationalDensity.IsSplitUnipotent.hasDenseRationalPoints`); `𝔾_m` has
  dense rational points by the published finite Galois splitting of tori
  (`IsTorus.hasDenseRationalPoints_of_finiteGaloisSplitting` with
  `torusFiniteGaloisSplitting`).
- `hasDenseRationalPoints`: over an infinite field, `D.group` has dense rational
  points, because a dominant power map from a finite power of the source has
  dense image (`hasDenseRationalPoints_of_denseRange`).

## Provenance

This is internal, derived content. In Conrad–Gabber–Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive
groups*, second edition (2015), source ID
`conrad-gabber-prasad-2015-pseudo-reductive`, the infinite-field case of
Lemma C.2.1 (printed pp.592–593) uses the subgroup generated by ground-field
tori, as recorded in the published Markdown of
`PseudoParabolicQuotientRationalLiftingStatement` and
`TorusGeneratedEnvelopeNormalityStatement`. The subgroup `H` constructed here
plays the same role in the lifting argument. Only its normalization by `P(χ)`
is used, so the normality of the torus-generated subgroup (CGP Proposition
A.2.11) is not needed.
